checks.finding: Requirements specify concrete, testable behaviors, explicit RFC 2119 keywords, and unambiguous verification criteria across all six requirements.
Complete bidirectional traceability exists between all stated goals, requirements REQ-001 through REQ-006, and acceptance criteria AC-001 through AC-014.
All acceptance criteria AC-001 through AC-014 define concrete, observable outcomes with designated test types and verification fixtures.

Workflow phase-sequencing violation: requirements.md line 21 cites 'see traceability.md for the observed drift' and investigation.md lines 53-54 and 60-61 reference design and traceability artifacts while Spec-Review-Status is Pending. Investigation.md lacks a conforming '## Amendment Re-Review Context' section required by calibration rules to permit references to downstream artifacts. This leaves implementers and task authors unable to determine whether Phase 1 specification is unapproved or whether downstream design and traceability artifacts are already authoritative. Under calibration rules, an unauthorized workflow boundary violation carries critical severity.

Technical, backward-compatibility, verification, and security constraints are explicitly stated with fail-closed requirements across REQ-001 through REQ-005 and the Security and Trust Boundaries section.
All identified risks are paired with concrete validation surfaces and acceptance tests (AC-001 through AC-014).
The specification strictly conforms to existing domain architecture, honoring ADR-0016, ADR-0017, and ADR-0018 without redefining or bypassing established boundaries.
